title: Sheaf descent is detected by degree-zero restriction
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site with pullbacks, $s:C\simeq C$ an equivalence with both directions continuous, $R$ a commutative ring sheaf, and $a:(s^{-1})^*R\simeq R$. Let $S:\operatorname{Site}(J,s,R,a)$, with copied-object category, inclusion $i$ and generated topology as in [def-sf-twisted-action-presentation-data]. Every set-valued presheaf $G$ on this copied-object category is an $S.\mathrm{topology}$-sheaf if $i^{\mathrm{op}}G$ is a $J$-sheaf. This is solely a sheaf criterion for an already constructed presheaf and asserts no extension or action-category equivalence.

proof.text: Prove the sheaf condition for the sieve image of any base sieve T whenever the restriction of G satisfies the sheaf condition for T. Restrict a matching family to the arrows inclusion.map f, glue in C, and use compatibility at an arbitrary factorization k followed by inclusion.map f to check amalgamation on the entire image sieve. Uniqueness follows on the base arrows. This argument is the private helper sheafFor_image.

Every integer power of s is continuous, by induction on natural powers of s and s inverse using Functor.isContinuous_comp. The identity law and arrows_comp imply that powerComp(0,n) and powerComp(n,0) are identity maps, with the integer-index transports recorded as heterogeneous equalities. For an arrow of degree n represented by g:Y to s^n X, pull the image of a J-cover T under (s^n).functor back along g. This is a J-cover by CoverPreserving.of_isContinuous and J.pullback_stable. If k belongs to it, factor k followed by g as q followed by (s^n).map l, with l in T. The degree-n arrow represented by q followed by inclusion.map l equals inclusion.map k followed by the original arrow, by arrows_comp and the degree-zero normalizations. Thus this base cover is contained in the base restriction of the pullback of the image sieve. J.superset_covering proves that this restriction is covering.

For any pullback Q of an image covering sieve, let U be its base restriction. The previous step makes U a J-cover, and the image of U is a subsieve of Q by Sieve.functorPullback_pushforward_le. The first step proves the sheaf condition on that subsieve. For any further arrow, the previous step gives a covering base restriction of its pullback; separatedness of the restricted sheaf therefore implies separatedness of G there. Every copied object is the image of its base object, by inclusion_obj. Apply Presieve.isSheafFor_subsieve_aux to obtain the sheaf condition on Q. Consequently every generating image sieve belongs to Sheaf.finestTopologySingle G. The sInf equation topology_eq gives S.topology less than or equal to this finest topology; Presieve.isSheaf_of_le and isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type yield the conclusion.

    letI := S.category
    ∀ (G : (Object C)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u),
      Presheaf.IsSheaf J (S.inclusion.op ⋙ G) → Presheaf.IsSheaf S.topology G
